Complete design with coded responses

complete_design.Rd

This function automatically completes missings for coded responses.

Usage

complete_design(
  coded,
  units,
  design,
  identifiers = c("group_id", "login_name", "login_code"),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  missings = NULL,
  recode_omissions_to_not_reached = FALSE,
  preserve_not_reached = FALSE
)

Arguments

coded

Tibble. Response data coded with code_responses(). The argument prepare must be TRUE.

units

Tibble. Unit data retrieved from the IQB Studio after setting the argument unit_definition = TRUE for get_units() – otherwise the page order of variables could not be correctly inferred from the variable source tree. Could already be treated by add_coding_scheme() to save some time.

design

Tibble. Design retrieved from Testcenter via get_design() or an object formatted in the same way.

identifiers

Character. Contains person identifiers of the dataset coded. Defaults to c("group_id", "login_name", "login_code") which corresponds to the identifiers of the IQB Testcenter.

overwrite

Logical. Should column unit_codes be overwritten if they exist on units. Defaults to FALSE, i.e., unit_codes will be used if they were added to units beforehand by applying add_coding_schemes().

missings

Tibble (optional). Provide missing meta data with code_id, code_status, code_score, and code_type. Defaults to NULL and uses default scheme. The supplied code_status is always preserved, including NA; the scheme assigns analytical codes and scores only.

recode_omissions_to_not_reached

Logical. Should trailing omissions (MISSING_BY_OMISSION) be recoded to not reached (MISSING_NOT_REACHED) when they occur at the end of a testlet? Defaults to FALSE.

preserve_not_reached

Logical. Should not-reached results be protected from recoding to omissions, even before later work? Defaults to FALSE. Protects supplied MISSING_NOT_REACHED types, the missing scheme's NR code when code_type is absent, and NR inferred during completion, including newly completed rows with code_status = NA. Other supplied types take precedence over a technical NOT_REACHED status or an NR code.

Value

A tibble including integer variable_position: the one-based position within unit_key used for sorting and missing classification, including derived variables. It is calculated from the unit metadata, replacing any input column of the same name. Positions can have gaps when design contains only part of a unit; variables absent from the unit metadata receive NA.

Details

Only variables explicitly linked to items in items_list (or item_metadata when items_list is absent), and their direct and indirect source variables, can establish the not-reached boundary. Own scores and variable names do not establish item relevance. After the existing code normalization, NO_CODING never establishes this boundary, even for items or their sources. Rows with a missing or blank item_id or variable_id are ignored without warning; whitespace-only values are also blank. An item list with nonblank item or variable identifiers but no complete links provides no boundary contributors. Missing or empty metadata, all-blank placeholders, conflicting complete links, or unresolvable required sources cause a unit-wide fallback: all variables in that unit may establish the boundary except NO_CODING. One aggregated warning identifies affected units. Unrelated design variables absent from coding metadata do not themselves trigger this fallback. Empty lists and all-blank placeholders cannot distinguish an item-free unit from missing metadata. This selection affects only the boundary. All design rows still receive the existing missing treatment; values, technical statuses, id_used, and the full-metadata ordering retain their previous treatment. Source evidence is evaluated at the source's own position, not the derived item's position.

Within each unit, base variables are ordered by numeric page, numeric section, and natural variable name (for example, V2 precedes V10). Missing sections follow known sections on the same page. Variables without a finite page follow known pages and are ordered by name alone. Derived variables with fully resolvable sources are inserted immediately after their last source, including chains of derivations. Simultaneously available derivations are ordered by natural name; their newly available dependants are inserted before the next sibling. Missing, ambiguous, or cyclic source links use the variable's own page, section, and name instead. Source links come from variable_sources, or from derive_sources when the former is empty. Element position and derivation level are not additional sorting keys. The trailing missing sequence is determined separately for each person, booklet, and testlet, including positions within a partly answered unit. Existing valid, invalid, and technical-error results retain their previous treatment; derived results are not reclassified from their source variables. An optional logical coding_from_not_reached column in coded records results produced by treating a known not-reached state as changed for coding. Only TRUE excludes that row from establishing the not-reached boundary; FALSE, NA, and an absent column retain the usual boundary treatment. This provenance does not itself change the row's code, score, or technical status, and is not propagated to derived results. A column of the same name in design is ignored; provenance is taken from coded only. A valid derived result included in the boundary can turn preceding not-reached sources into omissions unless preserve_not_reached = TRUE. Derived missing codes still follow the usual missing rules; no derivation is recalculated. Newly completed rows retain NA in code_status. The two missing options are independent: preserving NR does not turn inner omissions into NR. With both options TRUE, existing and newly inferred NR remain NR, and trailing omissions additionally become NR. Missing schemes still assign the corresponding codes and scores.
